### danafitkowski/cpp-cpm-engine
- URL: https://github.com/danafitkowski/cpp-cpm-engine
- Exact commit / revision: `6d9617d5d55b12372914ca0df08ff6b959048edf` (v2.9.44 release-evidence head; release engine commit `10dcc2c8f715f264e4868a581f2efe784e990b58`)
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: MIT, zero-runtime-dependency CPM and prospective Time Impact Analysis engine with calendar-aware FS/SS/FF/SF logic, constraints, actuals, out-of-sequence diagnostics, critical/driving path, free/total float, Primavera XER parsing, schedule-health primitives, AACE 29R-03 / 49R-06 / 52R-06 method labels, per-run manifests and topology fingerprints. `computeTIA` inserts one or more delay fragnets and returns baseline, per-fragnet impact in calendar/working days, cumulative extension and by-liability rollups.
- Rare or undernoticed value: This is not generic scheduling CRUD; it is explicitly built for reproducible forensic schedule analysis, with a Daubert disclosure posture, release evidence, CI attestations, 1,288 JS unit checks and JS/Python cross-validation. That gives ScopeSignal a credible schedule-dollar/entitlement-adjacent layer after a change has been proved.
- Likely buyer / user: Specialty contractors, GCs, claims consultants, project-controls teams, forensic schedulers and owners reviewing delay/EOT claims.
- Painful problem: A technically valid change can still lose substantial value if the contractor cannot show the schedule consequence on the accepted programme using transparent, reproducible math.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price change schedule-impact diagnostic: take a customer-authorized baseline/current XER plus a human-reviewed change fragnet and produce a reproducible impact appendix with methodology/provenance; later recurring change-monitoring or claims-prep infrastructure.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; compresses many months of CPM date math, calendar/constraint edge cases, P6 interoperability, TIA primitives, validation, provenance and expert-facing disclosure work.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact head/release commits; `README.md`; `docs/api.md`; `LICENSE`; release-evidence references; code-search evidence for Time Impact Analysis. README reports 1,288 JS checks, 1009/1015 JS↔Python comparisons (6 mutually unavailable completed-activity fields), 93% statement / 83% branch coverage, and openly discloses that a 282-activity real-XER stress test uses a non-public reference file. `docs/api.md` documents `computeTIA` isolated and cumulative-additive modes and its by-liability output.
- License / rights: MIT verified at the inspected revision. Project schedules and customer claim material remain customer-confidential inputs and require authorization.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT, with independent validation against the customer's scheduling environment before relying on conclusions.
- Why it is non-obvious: A low-attention specialist forensic engine whose valuable asset is evidentiary discipline and tested schedule math rather than a polished construction SaaS front end.
- Value score: **29/30** — A4, B5, C5, D5, E5, F5. Revenue can start as a diagnostic before full productization; business ceiling and build compression are high.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal reconciled PDF/CAD/IFC change -> OpenTakeoff quantity delta -> RFI Evidence Ledger contract/spec evidence -> contract-deadline agent notice preservation -> human-reviewed fragnet -> cpp-cpm-engine TIA -> BuildSuite/Massing/Procore change state and priced packet.
- Next action: Build one held-out benchmark that turns a rights-clean drawing/model change into a reviewed fragnet and tests whether the resulting TIA impact stays reproducible across an independently calculated schedule reference; do not auto-assign liability from geometry alone.

### BuildSuite-io/buildsuite_core
- URL: https://github.com/BuildSuite-io/buildsuite_core
- Exact commit / revision: `e18103efbbbec188f9fdea30cad27060a40aa4ad`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Actively maintained MIT construction operations layer for Frappe/ERPNext v16. The codebase connects project/work-package progress, FS/SS/FF scheduling, scope change orders, BOQ revisions, assemblies/rate history/cost codes, procurement, subcontract SOV/measurement books, retention/advance/net-payable billing, labour/plant costing and project P&L. Scope Change Order source includes Pending Approval/Approved/Rejected/Revise state transitions, mandatory rejection reasons, approver/date stamps and an immutable-style activity audit trail.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It supplies the downstream commercial operating spine missing from most change-detection projects. An approved scope change can explicitly be marked recoverable/absorbed, carry a currency impact, and raise a new BOQ revision linked back to the approved change rather than dying in a document folder.
- Likely buyer / user: Small/mid-market GCs, specialty contractors, EPC contractors and project-commercial teams already comfortable with ERPNext/Frappe.
- Painful problem: Even when extra scope is detected, contractors leak value when the change does not propagate into revised BOQ/cost-code state, measured subcontract work, billing and project margin.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price ScopeSignal-to-commercial-state integration for one contractor/project: import an evidence-backed candidate change into controlled approval, then carry accepted impact into BOQ revision and project cost/billing reporting.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; avoids rebuilding months of construction-specific document/state/accounting glue while deliberately leaving general accounting to ERPNext.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; root `README.md`; `license.txt`; `scope_change_order.py`; `scope_change_order.json`; `api/sco.py`; code-search hits for scope-change tests and progress reporting. The schema includes change type, currency impact, `recoverable`, status, reason, approval fields and linked BOQ revision; `create_boq_revision` refuses non-approved changes and duplicate revisions.
- License / rights: MIT verified in `license.txt`; Frappe/ERPNext and optional ecosystem dependencies retain their own licenses.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT subject to dependency obligations.
- Why it is non-obvious: It is positioned as an ERPNext contractor core, but the unusually valuable piece for ScopeSignal is the tested change -> approval -> BOQ revision -> cost/billing/accounting boundary.
- Value score: **28/30** — A4, B5, C5, D4, E5, F5. Slightly less rare than the forensic/revision engines, but exceptionally complete and commercially connected.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal evidence packet -> BuildSuite Scope Change Order -> human approval/rejection reason -> BOQ revision -> cost code/subcontract measurement -> invoice/P&L; pair with cpp-cpm-engine for schedule impact and contract-deadline-agent for notice preservation.
- Next action: Prototype a one-way importer that creates a Draft/Pending Scope Change Order from ScopeSignal evidence while preserving external revision IDs, quantity evidence and clause/RFI references, then measure whether accepted changes reach BOQ/billing without manual re-keying.

### HorizunGroup/horizun-msproject-mcp
- URL: https://github.com/HorizunGroup/horizun-msproject-mcp
- Exact commit / revision: `6761d8b86392c9b397c2d5adfbfdcb8591e421a8`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong
- What it contains: MIT MCP server that reads native MPP plus XER/MSPDI/PMXML and other schedules without requiring Microsoft Project or a JVM. It provides critical path/float, baseline comparison, DCMA-14, earned value, verified task/link/resource/calendar writes, dry-run impact simulation, schedule recovery/target/sequence/learning/generation, quantity-to-duration BIM linkage and 4D date export. Every reported write is re-read and verified.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The combination of native schedule-file access, verified writes, measured what-if recovery and BIM quantity/productivity linkage is directly relevant to turning a ScopeSignal quantity change into a schedule consequence without forcing customers into a new planning UI.
- Likely buyer / user: Construction planners, PMs, schedulers, project-controls teams and AI workflow vendors serving firms that use Microsoft Project/P6 exports.
- Painful problem: Change-impact analysis often requires brittle manual schedule edits, and automation can silently write impossible/calculated fields or reschedule imported programmes under different semantics.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Authorized schedule-change sandbox: inject a reviewed change assumption into a copy, report measured finish/critical-path movement and recovery alternatives, then hand the planner the verified delta rather than editing the live schedule.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; saves months of schedule-format I/O, concurrency controls, CPM/calendar work, write verification, DCMA checks and BIM/schedule bridging.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `README.md`; root MIT `LICENSE`; documented 209 end-to-end/scheduler/planning/robustness/smoke checks; explicit production-file testing; capability-honesty section. The project discloses that its scheduler reproduces imported Microsoft Project dates imperfectly on several real schedules (100%, 69%, ~23%, ~23%), so imported dates are preserved and recalculation is explicit rather than silent.
- License / rights: MIT verified. Input schedule rights/confidentiality remain with the customer; MPXJ and format dependencies retain their own terms.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT, with the disclosed imported-scheduler divergence treated as a hard validation constraint.
- Why it is non-obvious: A compact MCP server hides unusually rigorous verified-write and simulation semantics plus a construction-specific BIM productivity bridge.
- Value score: **27/30** — A4, B5, C5, D4, E4, F5. Evidence is strong, but imported Microsoft Project scheduler divergence prevents treating it as a forensic oracle.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal quantity delta -> task/BIM code mapping -> Horizun dry-run schedule impact/recovery -> cpp-cpm-engine independent TIA check -> human planner acceptance -> priced change state.
- Next action: Use it as an integration/simulation layer, not sole forensic truth: benchmark one authorized MPP/XER change against cpp-cpm-engine and the customer's native scheduler before promotion to a claims-facing workflow.

### TMailletFR/ProjectEngine
- URL: https://github.com/TMailletFR/ProjectEngine
- Exact commit / revision: `b92967dd13fd87fac977dbcdd169fc549be350f4` (v1.2.7)
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: GPL-3.0 dependency-driven scheduling/project-controls engine implemented in native Excel/VBA. It calculates FS/SS/FF networks, positive/negative lag, calendars, constraints, critical/longest paths, total/free float, driving logic, deadline exposure, baseline/forecast variance, diagnostics, S-curves and non-destructive TEST/SCENARIO simulation with controlled LOCK/rollback.
- Rare or undernoticed value: Gives Excel-native contractor teams real schedule propagation and controlled what-if testing without forcing a new enterprise scheduler, useful as a validation/adoption surface for ScopeSignal schedule impact.
- Likely buyer / user: Contractors, EPC/industrial teams and PMO/project-controls groups that live in Excel and lack P6/MS Project access.
- Painful problem: Static Excel Gantts hide successor movement, critical-path changes and deadline exposure after a scope/duration change.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: GPL-compliant implementation/training or export of ScopeSignal-reviewed duration deltas into a scenario workbook for client-side schedule review.
- Build-time / data advantage: High for Excel-native scheduling/reporting; lower for forensic claims because it lacks cpp-cpm-engine's expert disclosure/provenance posture.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `README.md`; root contents; `LICENSE.txt`; active September 2026 hotfix history. README documents scheduling engine, diagnostics, scenario/lock flows and stable state, while v1.2.7 fixed zero-dependency edge cases reported from real-world testing.
- License / rights: GPL-3.0 verified; distribution/modification requires GPL compliance.
- Reuse classification: Reusable under GPL conditions; otherwise architecture/validation reference.
- Why it is non-obvious: A large Excel/VBA project controls engine is easy to dismiss as a template, but it contains an actual calculation/simulation engine and operational diagnostics.
- Value score: **23/30** — A3, B4, C4, D3, E5, F4. Strong completeness, but copyleft and overlap with stronger forensic/schedule engines keep it in watch.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal accepted change -> Excel TEST/SCENARIO duration adjustment -> planner-visible critical/longest path and deadline delta -> formal TIA in cpp-cpm-engine if the claim advances.
- Next action: Retain as an Excel adoption/validation option; do not prioritize over cpp-cpm-engine + Horizun unless a target customer requires Excel-native review.

### resuly/daleads-mcp
- URL: https://github.com/resuly/daleads-mcp
- Exact commit / revision: `30dd22d1f7faba4ed213c1a3fe9a8d9593af6b26`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch / clean-room architecture reference
- What it contains: MCP/API contract for Australian development applications plus canonical project/property intelligence. Search/project tools expose stage/type/change-since filters, durable project change cursors, nearby projects, idempotent watches, and a `current_snapshot` model with per-field observed/conflict/multiple/not-captured/withheld states, evidence URLs/dates/pages/precision/basis/attribution, delivery states and rights-gated provenance. DA records expose council/category/status/lodgement/cost/dwelling/building facts while intentionally excluding applicant names.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The interesting asset is not the paid data itself but the disciplined evidence-and-rights state model: a project fact can be observed, conflicted, withheld or only partially provenance-delivered instead of being flattened into a confident sales lead. That is a strong pattern for PermitPlate's higher-value project intelligence.
- Likely buyer / user: Construction sales teams, suppliers, developers, planners, property analysts and agent builders working with Australian DA/property data.
- Painful problem: Permit/development feeds become stale or misleading when independent applications are not resolved into durable projects and when field-level provenance/rights/coverage are not preserved.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: For PermitPlate, independently reproduce the evidence/delivery-state contract on rights-clean U.S. municipal sources and sell a project-watch feed that says what changed, why it is believed and which fields are withheld/uncertain. DA Leads itself is a paid external API, not our moat.
- Build-time / data advantage: Medium-high as an architecture reference; the actual hard-to-recreate Australian dataset remains behind the provider API.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `README.md`; recursive tree; `contracts/project-intelligence-v1.json`; `pyproject.toml`. The contract explicitly defines durable checkpoint vs continuation cursor semantics, project snapshot fact/evidence fields, conflict/not-captured/withheld states and delivery/provenance states.
- License / rights: No repository-wide license file and no package license declaration found at the inspected revision. Provider API data is entitlement/rights gated.
- Reuse classification: Inspect/learn/clean-room only unless an explicit license is established; provider data may be used only under its service terms/entitlements.
- Why it is non-obvious: A small MCP client exposes a sophisticated lawful-public-data product contract that is more valuable to us as a design pattern than as code.
- Value score: **21/30** — A3, B4, C4, D4, E5, F1. Rights block code reuse, but the project/evidence contract is unusually instructive.
- Combination opportunities: Urban Signal + Accela/Revitalize collectors -> canonical property/project resolver -> PermitSignal/ParcelProof evidence objects -> DA-Leads-style per-field conflict/withheld/delivery state -> buyer-specific opportunity score and project watch.
- Next action: Implement a minimal independent `current_snapshot` contract for one PermitPlate city and test whether permit/project changes can retain source/date/field precision and explicit conflict/withheld state through scoring.

### ZetriSofu40/odoo-amc-maintenance-management
- URL: https://github.com/ZetriSofu40/odoo-amc-maintenance-management
- Exact commit / revision: `15810b9429a97bc62c2efa1e41ea83c46d0a1daf`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: LGPL-3 Odoo 15-19 Annual Maintenance Contract engine for facilities/HVAC/MEP/fire-safety/security/elevator/IT service. It models contract plans, inclusions/exclusions, covered assets, service frequency, call allowance, priority SLA, signed agreements/renewals, idempotent preventive schedules, reactive response/resolution deadlines, work-order checklists, labour/parts/photos/findings/root cause/corrective action/recommendations, customer signature, service reports, contract billing and uncovered extra-work invoicing.
- Rare or undernoticed value: This directly solves the field-service Proof-to-Cash/contract-leakage authority layer the queue calls for: not merely 'work completed', but whether the job was covered, what evidence/customer acceptance exists, and what labour/parts should become an extra invoice rather than being silently absorbed under the AMC.
- Likely buyer / user: HVAC, fire/life-safety, elevator, security, MEP and other recurring-service contractors with annual/comprehensive maintenance agreements.
- Painful problem: Completed reactive/extra work often leaks margin because coverage, allowance, evidence and invoicing are disconnected; the inverse risk is billing work that should have been included in contract coverage.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price contract-leakage audit on 50-200 closed work orders: reconcile each job to active AMC scope/coverage/allowance, customer sign-off and billed extras, then quantify completed-but-unbilled uncovered work and possibly misclassified covered work. Recurring leakage monitor after validation.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; saves months of service-contract scope, preventive/reactive lifecycle, SLA, evidence/signature, invoice/renewal and multi-version Odoo domain work.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; root `README.md`; root `LICENSE`; Odoo 19 module tree; `tests/test_amc_workflow.py`. Tests prove duplicate-safe schedule generation; reactive SLA deadlines and lifecycle; refusal to complete before checklist/signature; service-report rendering; contract billing; an extra-work invoice with $150 extra labour + two $200 billable parts = $550 draft invoice; renewal scope continuity without copying service history; reader write denial.
- License / rights: LGPL-3 verified. Commercial use is possible subject to LGPL obligations and Odoo/dependency terms. Customer service records/contracts remain confidential.
- Reuse classification: Reusable under LGPL-3 with deliberate separation/compliance; alternatively a strong domain test/reference corpus.
- Why it is non-obvious: A zero/very-low-attention Odoo add-on contains the exact entitlement-to-proof-to-invoice workflow that generic CMMS hunts repeatedly miss.
- Value score: **28/30** — A5, B5, C5, D4, E5, F4. The paid wedge is immediate and measurable; rights are clear though not permissive.
- Combination opportunities: cmms-normalize -> AMC contract/coverage resolver -> existing CAFM/field proof -> customer checklist/signature -> uncovered-extra invoice candidate -> Beveren-style completed-unbilled/margin analysis -> FM-DispatchBench for technician optimization.
- Next action: Build a rights-clean benchmark dataset of synthetic AMC contracts + work orders where coverage/allowance/sign-off/billing truth is known, then test detection of unbilled extras and wrongly billed covered work before building any integration.
